scope: Installed public operation documentation; does not certify an existing project's readiness

documents.reference:
% Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand
% Please edit documentation in R/project.R
\name{project}
\alias{project}
\title{Create an offline research project scaffold}
\usage{
project(
  name,
  type,
  goal,
  path = getwd(),
  config = NULL,
  options = list(),
  dry_run = FALSE
)
}
\arguments{
\item{name}{Nonempty project title, kept as written. A portable
child-directory slug is derived once: ASCII transliteration where
possible; when letters have no transliteration (for example CJK script) or
the slug would exceed 80 characters, a short hash of the name is appended
(\verb{project_<hash>} when nothing transliterates).}

\item{type}{One of \code{primary_research}, \code{secondary_research}, \code{methods},
\code{review}, \code{software}, \code{mixed}, or \code{other}.}

\item{goal}{Nonempty research objective.}

\item{path}{Existing parent directory; never the project directory itself.}

\item{config}{Optional named configuration list or local JSON/YAML file.}

\item{options}{Named configuration list taking precedence over \code{config}.}

\item{dry_run}{If TRUE, return a plan without writing any files.}
}
\value{
A \code{cttir_project} containing path, spec, plan, readiness, manifest and
warnings. An identical repeat is read-only and preserves user edits.
\code{readiness$level} becomes \code{environment_ready} only when \code{renv.lock} and the
project library match the pinned dependencies; \code{readiness$environment} and
\code{readiness$git} report the evidence and any recovery command. The
environment state is derived on each machine from \code{renv.lock}, the project
library and \code{.cttir/environment.json}; \code{cttir-lock.json} pins versions but
never records an installed environment.
\code{readiness$analysis} reports candidate routing, missing fields and capability
gaps. It never opens data or executes a model, even with \code{analysis$approved}.
}
\description{
The foundation build uses deterministic templates, without package
installation or execution of study code. It makes no network calls and no
model inference unless the local planner policy enables one loopback
exchange with an owned local model (see Details). The planned
standard workflow uses the reviewed reflowR layout. Advanced workflow
options that are not implemented raise a typed error instead of being ignored.
}
\details{
Explicit \code{workflow} options add reviewed integrations. \code{pipeline = "targets"}
writes \verb{_targets.R} and adds targets to the dependency manifest.
\code{environment = "renv"} with \code{prepare_environment = TRUE} prepares a project
library in an isolated R process after the scaffold has been published,
honoring \code{network} (\code{"offline"} by default). \code{git = TRUE} runs \verb{git init} in
the new project root only, never inside another work tree, and never stages
or commits. Failures of these steps keep the scaffold and are reported as
readiness blockers with a recovery command.
\code{reporting = "workflowr"} with \code{git = TRUE} creates one root workflowr site.
\code{reporting_preset} selects \code{"minimal"} or \code{"standard"} (default). Rendering
is explicit and checks current computation receipts. Use \code{\link[=sync]{sync()}} to preview
migration from the current generic bundle. With workflowr, targets scheduling
checks content identities and reuses fresh study results before explicit rendering.

Creation stages the scaffold next to the target and publishes it with one
rename while holding a creation lock that records its process. A lock left
by a stopped process on this host (or an ownerless lock from an older
version, after 24 hours) is recovered on the next attempt: only the lock and
that attempt's staging directory are removed, and \code{recovered} reports it.

Optional \code{analysis$mapping} records \code{data_source_id}, \code{outcome},
\code{predictors}, \code{subject}, \code{time}, \code{event}, \code{event_value}, \code{non_event_value},
\code{estimand}, \code{time_origin}, \code{time_unit} and \code{missing_data}. Dataset IDs must
refer to \code{data_sources}. Column names are literal data, not R expressions.
An explicitly empty predictor list denotes an intercept-only intention.
Missing-data choices are \code{unknown}, \code{fail} and \code{complete_case}; these record
intent and never remove observations during planning. Predictive and causal
designs are marked as requiring additional supported adapters. Scientific
and revision-specific workflow approval remain separate prerequisites.

Unset aim, outcome family, unit structure and modality are filled from goal
keywords by default. Only when \code{options(cttiR.planner = "local_llm")} is
set and the owned runtime prepared by \code{\link[=setup]{setup()}} and its recorded model
digest verify, one bounded read-only exchange with that local model (at
most one repair) proposes the same unset fields, also in dry runs. It never
starts, pulls or installs anything; explicit values always win; failures
fall back to the keyword rules, and replies showing signs of embedded
instructions leave the fields unknown. The reason is recorded in
\code{spec$decisions}.
}
\examples{
p <- project("Example", "methods", "Plan a reproducible comparison",
  path = tempdir(), dry_run = TRUE
)
print(p)
}
